key_insight: FlashAttention-4 co-designs attention algorithms with kernel-level pipelining to match asymmetric hardware characteristics of Blackwell GPUs (B200/GB200), delivering much higher sustained attention throughput and utilization than prior H100-optimized methods.
problem_solved: Existing FlashAttention variants were tuned for Hopper (H100) microarchitecture; they underutilize or misbalance compute, memory and tensor-core resources on Blackwell-class GPUs, creating an attention bottleneck for large models and long contexts.
method: Algorithm–kernel co-design: restructure attention computation into pipelined stages that expose overlapping compute and memory operations tailored to Blackwell asymmetries.
Asymmetric tiling and warp specialization: adapt tile sizes, work distribution, and tensor-core usage per stage/SM to match imbalanced compute vs. bandwidth on B200/GB200.
Autotuning and scheduler-aware kernels: runtime selection of pipeline depth, kernel ordering and buffer lifetimes to maximize utilization across different sequence lengths and hardware variants.
impact: Practitioners get higher throughput and lower attention latency on modern Blackwell GPUs without redesigning models—enabling larger context windows and more cost-effective LLM inference/training on current hardware.
visual_elements: Pipeline timeline diagram showing overlapped kernel stages (load → compute → reduce → write) versus non-pipelined execution.
Comparative bar chart: throughput/latency for FlashAttention-3 vs FlashAttention-4 on H100 and B200/GB200 (no numeric labels required, emphasize relative improvement).
Hardware-to-algorithm mapping: schematic of asymmetric tiling and warp assignment across SMs/TensorCores.
Heatmap of SM utilization and memory-bandwidth pressure before vs after co-design highlighting balanced resource use.
paper_title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
paper_authors: Ted Zadouri, Markus Hoehnerbach, Jay Shah, Timmy Liu, Vijay Thakkar
